source: Three keys in one. (1) Juice Shop marks its own vulnerable lines with `// vuln-code-snippet vuln-line <challenge>`; `challengeRules` maps the challenges whose kind of problem Defuse checks, and every other marked challenge is out of scope. (2) data/static/codefixes holds the snippets its coding challenges show players: a file ending `_correct` is the fixed version, every other variant is vulnerable by Juice Shop's own answer. (3) `entries`: proofs outside those, read against the source by Claude on 2026-10-31.
expectProofWhy: restfulXssChallenge prints a product description read back from the API - stored data, so a fair guess is the right label and a proof is not expected.

entries.cause: database read treated as the request value
entries.note: The line is a real bug - Juice Shop's SSTI challenge, a username saved earlier and evaluated here - but the proof says the login cookie reaches eval, through findByPk(). The value that arrives is a stored username: second-order, which this engine does not follow.

entries.cause: SSRF claimed for code running in the browser

entries.note: localXssChallenge: the search query from the address bar, passed to bypassSecurityTrustHtml. Proven since Angular's route parameters and bypass calls were added (2026-11-01).

httpHeaderXssChallenge: the True-Client-IP header is saved at login (routes/saveLoginIp.ts), travels back in the JWT kept in localStorage, and is printed through bypassSecurityTrustHtml. The proof starts at localStorage - where the value comes from in the browser; the attacker writes it through the header.
